text.p: + Recent chart break by Scottish & Newcastle shares above 710p following a basically flat performance for over a year implies they are capable of marching on to 850p over the medium-term, technical analysts said.
+ A chart of the share price divided by the All-Share index has also broken above a 12 month downtrend to confirm the positive view. The shares will go ex-dividend on August 4.
Shares in brewer Scottish & Newcastle look set to overcome resistance at 770p and climb to record highs, technical analysts said.
"Medium-term, I can envisage a steady move to the 850p area," said Richard Lake, technical analyst at Brewin Dolphin & Co.
By 1030 GMT, S&N shares were up 2-1/2p to 730-1/2p.
Since 1996 the stock has been shuffling along between 620p-710p so that relative to the All-Share index -- which has been charging higher -- S&N shares have been underperforming by eight percent.

A sudden burst of energy from June this year took S&N shares past their 710p resistance in a near 140p advance to peak at 766p but share price volatility then made the stock retrace 38 percent of that 140p rise and the shares have been trying to find their feet since then.

These wild price fluctuations have made a daily chart of the shares take the formation of a symmetrical triangle pattern which consists of converging trendlines connecting the stock's highs and lows since mid-July.
The pattern usually represents a pause before the shares continue in their original direction prior to the pause.

A chart of S&N shares divided by the All-Share index has been in a downtrend since 1996 but recent buying interest in the shares has caused this relative performance line to break above the downtrend.
"Both price and relative (charts) have decisively broken major barriers of resistance," said Lake implying further upward moves for the stock.
The shares will go ex-dividend by 14.17p net on August 4.
